canonical_native_observations.clean_arm_controls: retry and parallelism disabled in both clean comparison arms

canonical_native_observations.reported_witness: parent runner failure followed by first-party recovery of the unfinished child under original child/dispatch identities while completed work remains closed and no replacement worker is created

reviewed_route_classes.blocking_reason: The benchmarks directly exercise whole-team current-control authority, but their management organization is authored by the benchmark rather than a canonical harness's own S3 path.

SupervisorAgent directly adds a live current-control loop around a base MAS and publishes a base-versus-SMAS result, but the S3 relation belongs to the composed supervised organization rather than the wrapped Smolagent/AWorld/OAgents boundary. The intervention repertoire also includes verification-like actions, so the aggregate result is not an isolated S3-only causal estimate and cannot form a canonical primary row.

Two canonical direct S3 observations now exist, but they are materially heterogeneous: Multi-Agent Orchestration publishes a controlled supervisor ablation on 54 scripted scenarios, while Omnigent publishes descriptive operational/regression evidence for parent/child recovery at a later post-assessment revision. They do not share a benchmark family, disturbance, model/configuration cell, metric or comparison protocol and therefore cannot form a primary cross-harness comparison.

The post-closure canonical admissions expose S3 current-control mechanisms, but current public result surfaces do not isolate those native paths in capability measurements. Their mechanism/performance/test evidence therefore does not add direct S3 observations.

The native Magentic-One and LLaMAR ablations change whole-team outcomes but do not isolate S3 as the measured variable. Magentic-One removes an orchestrator bundle spanning S2/S3, while LLaMAR changes Planner/Verifier/Corrector combinations and reports broad MAP-THOR end-task metrics. Both remain proxy evidence rather than direct S3 observations.
The matched campaign holds model/tools/workload fixed but evaluates Agno and AutoGen through benchmark-selected organization paths that are not the canonical S3 paths used to establish S3 ownership.
The benchmark directly studies orchestration failures and recovery, but public evidence does not bind the measurements to native canonical harness S3 implementations.

closure_claim: Current public evidence contains four direct S3 benchmark families, three admitted direct S3 observations and two native quantitative proxy projections. Multi-Agent Orchestration and Omnigent provide the two canonical direct observations; SupervisorAgent / SMAS adds one first-party-reported composed non-canonical observation. AutoGen/Magentic-One and LLaMAR add native proxy evidence but do not isolate S3. The canonical direct rows remain materially heterogeneous and the SMAS row belongs to a composed benchmark boundary, so no cross-harness canonical-native S3 primary baseline is currently supported.
reopen_when: a materially matched benchmark/model/configuration cell evaluates two or more canonical systems through their own native or adapter-preserved S3 paths
an existing matched framework campaign proves that canonical S3 paths are actually active for two or more systems under one recoverable comparison protocol
a new direct orchestration benchmark binds immutable, comparable results to multiple canonical native S3 implementations
do_not_reopen_for: another descriptive canonical S3 observation without a materially comparable cross-harness cell
another direct composed or benchmark-scaffolded S3 observation without canonical native or adapter-preserved linkage
another whole-task orchestration score without isolated current-control attribution
another framework comparison that does not activate canonical S3 paths
microperformance or mechanism tests that do not measure a current-control intervention and subsequent organizational outcome
non_claim: This closure is not a zero S3 capability score and does not normalize the heterogeneous Multi-Agent Orchestration, Omnigent, SMAS, Magentic-One or LLaMAR evidence into one metric or ranking. Omnigent's observation is explicitly post-assessment temporal evidence and does not rewrite the earlier canonical review revision. SupervisorAgent / SMAS is direct evidence only at the composed supervised-MAS boundary and does not transfer S3 ownership to wrapped systems. LLaMAR's module ablation remains proxy evidence and does not establish a direct S3 observation. The S3 primary remains gap until materially matched canonical-native evidence appears.
